pageDescription: Why your care provider uses DocNote: more presence in consultations, accurate notes, Swiss-hosted data, and you stay in control.

hero.title: What if your doctor could give you their full attention?
hero.subtitle: Why your care provider uses DocNote — and what it changes for you during every appointment.
hero.lead: Consultations are often interrupted by typing, clicking, and screen-staring. DocNote helps your care provider stay with you in the room: listening, explaining, and deciding — while a discreet assistant handles the notes they would otherwise write by hand.

story.title: Your appointment, without the keyboard between you
paragraphs: During your visit, your care provider may use DocNote — an assistant that records the conversation (only with your agreement), turns it into text, and drafts a structured clinical report.

They no longer need to split attention between you and a keyboard. They can look at you, ask follow-up questions, and explain the plan clearly. After the visit, they review the draft, correct anything that needs correcting, and validate it. Only that validated report becomes part of your medical file — just like any other consultation note.

benefits.title: A consultation that feels like a conversation again
benefits.subtitle: DocNote is built for clinicians — but the people who notice the difference first are often patients.

items.title: They are more present
items.body: Rather than staring at a screen and typing, your care provider listens and looks at you. The appointment becomes a real exchange: symptoms, worries, and decisions get the attention they deserve.

items.title: Nothing important is missed
items.body: The report faithfully captures what was said — your symptoms, your history, the options discussed, and the decisions made — so follow-ups start from a clearer shared record.

items.title: More time for your care
items.body: Hours that used to disappear into paperwork after clinic can return to patients. Shorter documentation time often means longer, calmer conversations when it matters.

items.title: Clearer notes for your next visit
items.body: A well-structured report helps the whole care team understand what happened last time. Continuity improves when the story of your care is accurate and easy to revisit.

steps.title: What happens with your appointment
steps.subtitle: Simple, transparent, and always under your care provider's responsibility.

items.title: You agree to the recording
items.body: Nothing starts without your consent. If you prefer not to use DocNote, say so — your care is unchanged.

items.title: The visit is transcribed
items.body: The conversation is converted into text, then into a draft clinical report. No one outside the automated process "listens in" on your appointment.

items.title: Your clinician reviews and validates
items.body: Your care provider reads the draft, corrects it if needed, and validates it. They remain solely responsible for your medical file.

items.title: Audio is deleted; the note stays
items.body: The audio recording is automatically deleted no later than 7 days after the appointment. Only the validated report is kept in your file.

quote.text: The original idea was simple: give care providers back the time and attention they owe their patients.
quote.attribution: DocNote — designed in Switzerland by a doctor

privacy.title: Built around medical secrecy
privacy.intro: Your health information deserves the same protection as the rest of your medical file — and DocNote is designed that way from the start.

points.title: Hosted in Switzerland
points.body: Your data stays in Switzerland, on Swiss servers, and does not leave the country for processing.

points.title: Never sold or used for ads
points.body: Your consultations are not a product. Data is never sold and never used for advertising.

points.title: Not used to train AI
points.body: Your visits are only used to produce your report. They are never used to train an artificial intelligence model.

points.title: Access limited to your care team
points.body: Only your care team can access your information, under medical secrecy — not insurers, employers, or advertisers.

control.title: You stay in control
control.body: You can refuse DocNote at any time, simply by telling your care provider, and this does not affect your care in any way. You can also ask them any questions you have. You have rights over your data under Swiss data protection law — including the right to know what data concerns you.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Straight answers about recording, responsibility, insurance, and your choices.

items.q: Does a human listen to my consultation?
items.a: No. Everything is automated — the recording is not listened to by anyone. Only your care provider accesses the report, which they read and validate.

items.q: What if the assistant makes a mistake?
items.a: No document reaches your file without review. Your care provider checks and corrects each report before validating it. Your medical file remains entirely under their responsibility.

items.q: Can my insurance company access it?
items.a: No. Your data is covered by medical secrecy and is not shared with anyone outside your care team — not your insurance, not your employer, not an advertiser.

items.q: Is my data used to train an AI?
items.a: No, never. It is only used to produce your report.

items.q: How long is the recording kept?
items.a: It is automatically deleted no later than 7 days after the consultation. Only the report validated by your care provider remains in your file.
Yes, at any time, and it does not affect the quality of your care.

DocNote was designed in Switzerland by a doctor, to fit the reality of medical care and respect the requirements of medical secrecy. The original idea was simple: give care providers back the time and attention they owe their patients.

cta.title: Still have a question?
cta.body: Talk to your care provider first — they know how DocNote is used in their practice. You can also write to us directly.
